question: What changed in the EU AI Act implementation timeline?
title: Changes in the EU AI Act Implementation Timeline

sentences.text: The General-Purpose AI (GPAI) Code of Practice was published on 10 July 2025, more than two months later than initially planned, while GPAI rules became applicable on 2 August 2025.
Regulation (EU) 2026/1744 entered into force on 27 July 2026, changing the timeline for Article 6(1)/Annex I and Article 6(2)/Annex III high-risk routes to later dates.
The majority of the EU AI Act's rules became applicable on 2 August 2026, with some exceptions.

According to a single source, the GPAI Code of Practice was initially expected by 2 May 2025, but its final version was published on 10 July 2025, more than two months later than initially planned.
The EU AI Act rules regarding General-Purpose AI became applicable starting from 2 August 2025.
Regulation (EU) 2026/1744 was published on 24 July 2026 and entered into force on 27 July 2026 to simplify the implementation of harmonised rules on artificial intelligence.
Regulation (EU) 2026/1744 changed the timeline for Article 6(2)/Annex III and Article 6(1)/Annex I high-risk routes, moving them to later dates.
A single source reports that a narrow Article 50(2) legacy-system transition ends on 2 December 2026.
Sources contest the timing of political agreement on the Digital Omnibus on AI, citing either 7 May 2026 or a provisional agreement on 6 May 2026 confirmed on 13 May 2026.

While GPAI rules took effect on 2 August 2025 following the release of the GPAI Code of Practice on 10 July 2025, the high-risk system timelines under Annex I and Annex III were postponed by Regulation (EU) 2026/1744.
The general rules of the AI Act became applicable on 2 August 2026, with specific transition periods and delegated act deadlines continuing into December 2026 and August 2027.

k14.statement: The European institutions reached a provisional political agreement on the Digital Omnibus on AI on 6 May 2026, which was confirmed by Member State representatives on 13 May 2026.

k18.statement: The European Commission is mandated to adopt delegated acts by 2 August 2027 to specify which high-risk AI systems may have limited application of specific requirements or obligations and the conditions for such limitations.

k19.statement: The European Parliament and Council enacted Regulation (EU) 2026/1744 on 8 July 2026, which amends the main AI Act (Regulation (EU) 2024/1689) to simplify the implementation of harmonised AI rules.

k20.statement: A new regulation, Regulation (EU) 2026/1744, was enacted to amend Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 (the EU AI Act) concerning the simplification of the implementation of harmonised rules on artificial intelligence.

k21.statement: The EU Commission published the GPAI Code of Practice on 10 July 2025.

k22.statement: The European Commission published the Digital Omnibus proposal on 19 November 2025 to address implementation issues in the AI Act.

k24.statement: The EU AI Act (Regulation (EU) 2024/1689) entered into force on 2 August 2024.

k25.statement: The European standard EN 18286:2026 concerning quality management systems for the EU AI Act was approved on 12 July 2026.
